fact: The gazetted Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 24 of 2023) was assented to by the President on 19 December 2023, bears the operative date 22 December 2023 and repeals the former Data Protection Act (Cap 57) in section 55; section 56 gives controllers and processors already processing data 18 months from commencement (to 22 June 2025) to conform.

Section 5 names the Information Commission, established under section 36 of the Access to Information Act, as the competent authority to enforce the Act, with powers to investigate, audit, issue enforcement notices and impose administrative fines up to SCR200,000; the document itself does not state that the Commission was acting under the Act.
The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Malabo Convention by Seychelles.
DLA Piper states the Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 24 of 2023) came into force on 22 December 2023, with oversight and enforcement through the Information Commission.
The CEO states the Data Protection Act was enacted in December 2023 and the first cases under it were received in early 2024, with the law described as new and still being established.

The Commission received four data protection cases in 2024, mostly from the non-banking financial sector, handled through investigations, consultations, mediation and recommendations, with no decision or sanction on a named controller reported.

The Information Commission, led by a Chief Information Commissioner with Information Commissioners and a CEO, administers the Data Protection Act 2023 alongside the Access to Information Act; it reports significant recruitment and staffing challenges for the new Act.
The report states the Commission administered the Data Protection Act 2023 during 2025, handling 14 cases under it, and that implementation continued to gain momentum.

The Commission received and handled 14 cases under the Act in 2025 (6 data transfers, 5 breaches, 2 refused deletion requests, 1 consultation), described as guidance, assessment and corrective advice, with no decision or sanction on a named controller and no count of cases settled.

The Information Commission, with a Chief Information Commissioner, two Information Commissioners and a CEO in post, administers and oversees the Data Protection Act 2023 and reports annually under its section 12(2).
Seychelles Nation reports the National Assembly approved the Data Protection Bill 2023 on 5 December 2023, and says nothing of it being in force.
